defense_analyst.prose: BUF's defense has allowed -0.03 EPA per play [dc1] over 625 plays [dc2], ranking 10th in the league [dc3], with a 44.0% success rate allowed [dc4]. The Bills blitz often: they send 5+ rushers on 35.3% of dropbacks [dc5] over 411 dropbacks [dc6], averaging 4.39 rushers per dropback [dc7], and their pressure proxy is 20.4% [dc8] with a 5.6% sack rate [dc9]. KC has protected well by comparison, with a pressure proxy of 16.6% [dc10] and a sack rate of 3.5% [dc11]. KC's passing game is the main threat at 0.19 EPA per pass play [dc12] over 367 pass plays [dc13], and it leans pass on early downs, ranking 16th highest in early-down pass rate [dc14]. Expect BUF to be in coverage often on early downs, so the pressure plan has to be picked against KC's quick game. The run game is less dangerous: KC gains 0.07 EPA per run [dc17] over 249 runs [dc18], and BUF's run boxes average 6.75 defenders [dc15] over 213 run plays [dc16]. KC's pass explosive rate is 9.0% [dc19] against BUF's allowed explosive rate of 8.6% [dc20], so deep shots are a real risk. On third down BUF allows 34.6% conversions [dc21] over 127 plays [dc22], while KC converts 42.1% [dc23] over 121 plays [dc24]. In the red zone BUF has allowed touchdowns on 59.4% of drives [dc25] over 32 drives [dc26], and KC has scored on 65.8% [dc27] over 38 drives [dc28]; both are small samples, but the red zone is where KC's offense is most dangerous.

The Bills blitz often, sending five or more rushers on 35.3% [dc5] of dropbacks over 411 [dc6], with a pressure proxy of 20.4% [dc8]. KC has protected better, with a pressure proxy allowed of 16.6% [dc10]. KC's passing game is the main threat at 0.19 [dc12] EPA per pass play over 367 [dc13] pass plays, and Buffalo should expect to sit in coverage on early downs. KC's pass explosive rate of 9.0% [dc19] meets Buffalo's allowed explosive rate of 8.6% [dc20], so deep shots are a real risk. On third down Buffalo allows 34.6% [dc21] conversions over 127 [dc22] plays, while KC converts 42.1% [dc23] over 121 [dc24]. In the red zone Buffalo has allowed touchdowns on 59.4% [dc25] of drives over 32 [dc26], and KC has scored on 65.8% [dc27] over 38 [dc28].

sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: Tyler Bass has made 24 [kc1] of 25 [kc2] field goals, 96.0% [kc3] over 25 [kc4] attempts, and he is the only kicker logged all season. Long tries are a thinner sample at 80.0% [kc5] on 5 [kc6] attempts. Buffalo's net punting is 43.6 [kc7] yards on 22 [kc8] punts, with 40.9% [kc9] landing inside the 20, so expect long fields after Buffalo punts. Kickoffs are rarely touchbacks, at 10.1% [kc10] across 69 [kc11] kicks. KC averages 26.6 [kc12] yards on 35 [kc13] returns, and Buffalo allows 26.6 [kc14] yards on 60 [kc15] returns, so the return matchup is even. KC's kicker is 66.7% [kc18] on 21 [kc19] attempts, so KC should not assume a long field goal is automatic late in games.

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: Buffalo TE Dalton Kincaid is listed as Doubtful, and he has 14.3% [ic3] of Bills targets over 287 [ic4] team targets. CB Christian Benford is Out, LB Dorian Williams is Out, and S Damar Hamlin is Questionable, so expect backups on the outside and more deep help. Kansas City RB Kenneth Walker III is Out. He carries 63.9% [ic10] of Chiefs rushes over 249 [ic11] team rushes, so the run game shifts to backups. G Trey Smith and T Jaylon Moore are also Out, thinning interior and tackle depth against the Bills' rush.

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: Third-and-long is the first deciding spot. Buffalo throws on 91.8% [mc1] of third-and-long snaps over 49 [mc2] plays, so KC must finish drives with its rush, using a sack rate of 5.2% [mc3] and pressure proxy of 13.2% [mc4]. Keep the rush in the pocket and cover Shakir and Moore, who draw 18.8% [mc5] and 16.7% [mc6] of targets. Second is pass protection against the blitz. Buffalo sends five or more rushers on 35.3% [mc7] of dropbacks over 411 [mc8]. With Smith and Jaylon Moore out, use quick game, hot throws and a back in protection, building off 0.19 [mc13] EPA per pass play over 367 [mc14] plays. Third is Cook, who carries 74.1% [mc15] of Buffalo's designed rushes, while KC loses Kenneth Walker III, who had 63.9% [mc17] of Chiefs carries. Stay balanced to keep Cook off the edge, but don't force early runs with backups. Fourth is the deep ball. Christian Benford is out after averaging 85.6% [mc20] of snaps per game, so take shots when Buffalo's safety help is thin.
